Before you go

  • Book refundable hotels (Reykjavík Thu, Hella Fri–Sat) and note each cancellation deadline. Options in 🏨 Where to stay below.
  • Blue Lagoon 9:30 slot. Cancel 24 h+ before = full refund; under 24 h = no refund. Changes may cost more (dynamic pricing). If they close for weather or an eruption, their terms say no refund is owed, so consider travel insurance. terms
  • Friðheimar 2 PM table on Dineout.
  • Blue Car: pick the refundable rate (free cancellation more than 24 h before pickup; confirm when booking). Ask for studded tires and a booster seat.

Thu · Nov 26

Land, lagoon, Reykjavík

≈ 45 mi (70 km) on the map route

🚗 1 h 18 driving (plan 1 h 55) · 👀 2 h 15 sights +45 min optional · 🛏 Reykjavík
☀️ Sunrise–sunset 10:31 AM – 3:57 PM · usable light 9:23 AM – 5:05 PM

  • ✈16:45 AMLand at KEF. Passport + bags ≈ 1 h
  • ✈17:45 AMBreakfast + coffee at the airport before you drive
  • ✈18:15 AMWalk 4 min to Blue Car Rental. Car + booster seat
  • 29:30 AMBlue Lagoon soak (book the 9:30 slot)🚗 21 min · plan 30 minOnly about 20 min of driving to get here.
  • 212:00 PMShower, then lunch at the lagoon (Lava opens 11:30)
  • 212:50 PM😴 Rest 20–30 min in the lagoon café/lounge or nap in the parked car. Warm water makes you sleepy
  • 🏠32:30 PMHotel check-in + rest. This is today's priority🚗 48 min · plan 1 h 05Standard check-in is usually 3 PM, so request early check-in when you book (it may cost extra). If the room isn't ready, leave your bags.
  • 44:00 PMIf you have energy: Hallgrímskirkja tower (last entry 4:45 PM) OR Perlan (open to 9 PM). Not both optional🚗 5 min · plan 10 min
  • 🏠35:30 PMEarly dinner, early bed🚗 5 min · plan 10 min
🌧 Bad-weather plan
  • Lagoon closed (eruption) or too tired: drive KEF → Reykjavík (45 min · plan 1 h).
  • Swim at Laugardalslaug instead: big outdoor pool, hot tubs, slides. Open Thu 6:30 AM–10 PM.
  • Perlan is indoors, so it works in any weather. Good if the room isn't ready yet.
  • Sky Lagoon is 12+ only, so it's not an option for your son.
⏩ Skip first if late
  • The optional tower/Perlan stop. Rest matters more today.
⚠️ Safety
  • You just flew overnight. Keep today's driving short and sleep early.
  • Blue Lagoon can close at very short notice if Sundhnúkur erupts. Check bluelagoon.com and safetravel.is that morning.
  • Floaties are required up to age 8 (free). One adult can bring at most two kids.
😴 Too tired to drive?
  • Feel drowsy at any point? Pull over in a safe spot (a parking lot or gas station) and rest. Don't push on.
  • Alternative: sleep near the lagoon or airport Thursday night instead. There are hotels in Reykjanesbær/Keflavík, and the Blue Lagoon has its own hotels (Silica, Retreat).
  • If you do, leave by about 8:15 AM Friday. KEF area → Þingvellir is 1 h 19 map, plan 1 h 45.
  • Less convenient option: take a taxi or Flybus from KEF and pick up the car later. Blue Car Rental is at KEF, so you'd have to come back to the airport for it.

Fri · Nov 27

Golden Circle → Hella

≈ 130 mi (205 km) on the map route

🚗 3 h 14 driving (plan 4 h 25) · 👀 2 h 10 sights +20 min optional · 🛏 Hella
☀️ Sunrise–sunset 10:30 AM – 3:46 PM · usable light 9:20 AM – 4:56 PM

  • 18:50 AMLeave Reykjavík (still dark)
  • 210:00 AMÞingvellir morning visit, rift walk. Sunrise ≈ 10:30🚗 46 min · plan 1 h
  • 312:15 PMGullfoss, upper viewpoint only optional🚗 1 h 08 · plan 1 h 30Skip it if you leave Þingvellir after 10:45. Drive straight to Geysir instead (59 min · plan 1 h 20).
  • 412:55 PMGeysir + Strokkur, snack at Geysir Center🚗 9 min · plan 15 min
  • 52:00 PMFriðheimar greenhouse lunch (2 PM table)🚗 17 min · plan 25 minConfirm the booking before you fix the order. Earlier table (11:30–12:30)? Swap to Þingvellir → Friðheimar → Geysir → Gullfoss → Hella (3 h 22 driving).
  • 🏠64:20 PMHotel near Hella, around dusk🚗 54 min · plan 1 h 15Tonight: check the Sat night/Sun forecast and decide on the Sunday storm backup (see Sunday 🌪).
🌧 Bad-weather plan
  • Storm or roads yellow/red: skip Gullfoss and go Þingvellir → Geysir → Friðheimar → Hella.
  • Very bad: skip Þingvellir too. Take Route 1 Reykjavík → Selfoss → Hella (about 1 h 30 base) and stop at Friðheimar if open.
  • Hellisheiði pass (Route 1) sometimes closes. When it does, Route 39 (Þrengsli) is the usual detour, if open.
⏩ Skip first if late
  • Gullfoss
  • Long Þingvellir walk: just see the viewpoint (15 min)
⚠️ Safety
  • Gullfoss: use the upper paths. The lower path is often roped off in winter. Respect the ropes.
  • Geysir: stay behind the ropes. The water is boiling.
  • Wear microspikes on all paths today.
  • Buy tomorrow's packed lunch and snacks this evening (Hella has a grocery store).

Sat · Nov 28

South Coast, back to Hella

≈ 130 mi (210 km) on the map route

🚗 3 h 18 driving (plan 4 h 35) · 👀 1 h 15 sights +1 h optional · 🛏 Hella
☀️ Sunrise–sunset 10:17 AM – 3:49 PM · usable light 9:11 AM – 4:56 PM

  • 🏠18:30 AMFill the tank in Hella (or Hvolsvöllur, 15 min on). Packed lunch in the car
  • 29:40 AMSeljalandsfoss, front view only🚗 32 min · plan 45 min
  • 310:55 AMSkógafoss, walk up close🚗 29 min · plan 40 min
  • 311:25 AMPacked lunch in the car at Skógar
  • 412:10 PMSólheimajökull glacier viewpoint optional🚗 13 min · plan 20 minIncludes the walk from the parking lot: about 1 km, roughly 15–20 min each way on an icy path. Short on time? Skip it.
  • 51:50 PMReynisfjara beach, from up high🚗 29 min · plan 40 minStay well back from the waves and obey any closure posts or staff.
  • 62:40 PMVík: red-roof church view, restroom optional🚗 12 min · plan 20 minSkip it if you're running late. Weather or roads getting worse? Turn back sooner, after Reynisfjara or even after Skógafoss.
  • 62:50 PM⏰ Head back. 3:00 PM is the latest you leave Vík
  • 🏠14:40 PMBack in Hella, before full dark (~5 PM)🚗 1 h 22 · plan 1 h 50
🌧 Bad-weather plan
  • Weather or roads getting worse? Turn back sooner. After Reynisfjara you're back in Hella about 4:00 PM. After Skógafoss, about 12:55 PM.
  • Short day: Hella → Seljalandsfoss → Skógafoss → Hella. That's 1 h 57 base, plan 2 h 40.
  • Wind warning (orange/red on vedur.is): stay in Hella and rest. If it calms by midday, just do Seljalandsfoss (45 min each way).
  • Reynisfjara closure posts, staff or red light: don't go down to the beach. Skip it.
  • Storm warning for Sat night/Sun morning (you decided Friday)? Do Seljalandsfoss + Skógafoss only, then drive west in daylight. See Sunday 🌪.
⏩ Skip first if late
  • Vík
  • Sólheimajökull
  • Reynisfjara (turn back after Skógafoss)
⚠️ Safety
  • Reynisfjara: dry sand is NOT safe. Sneaker waves can run far up the beach without warning. Stay well back from the shoreline (view from the top of the beach or the parking area), never turn your back to the sea, and hold your son's hand. If there's a closure post, staff, a red light or a warning, skip the beach entirely.
  • Seljalandsfoss: the path behind the falls is closed in winter (ice, falling icicles).
  • Sólheimajökull: only go as far as the viewpoint. Never step onto the glacier without a certified guide.
  • This is the longest day. Bring water, snacks and a power bank.

Sun · Nov 29

Kerið, then fly home

≈ 95 mi (155 km) on the map route

🚗 2 h 23 driving (plan 3 h 10) · 👀 0 min sights +20 min optional · 🛏 Flight home
☀️ Sunrise–sunset 10:30 AM – 3:48 PM · usable light 9:21 AM – 4:57 PM

  • 🏠19:30 AMCheck out, leave Hella
  • 210:40 AMKerið crater rim walk optional🚗 47 min · plan 1 h 05
  • ✈31:10 PMFill the tank in Reykjanesbær🚗 1 h 35 · plan 2 h 05
  • ✈31:20 PMReturn car at Blue (target 1:00–1:30 PM)
  • ✈31:45 PMCheck in, bag drop, security
  • ✈34:30 PMFly home
🌧 Bad-weather plan
  • Any doubt about the weather or roads: skip Kerið and drive straight to KEF.
  • Direct Hella → KEF: 1 h 59 base, plan 2 h 40. Leaving at 9:30 puts you at the car return about 12:20 PM. In a storm, allow 3 h+.
  • Leave by 9:30 either way. Arriving early at KEF beats missing the flight.
⏩ Skip first if late
  • Kerið
⚠️ Safety
  • Kerið's rim and stairs are often icy, and the edges aren't fenced. Wear spikes.
  • Check umferdin.is before you leave for Hellisheiði and Route 41.
🌪 Storm backup: decide Friday evening
  • Hella → KEF crosses Hellisheiði (Route 1), which can close in storms. The detour, Þrengsli (Route 39), can close too.
  • Friday evening: check en.vedur.is warnings and the Sat night/Sun forecast, plus umferdin.is.
  • Yellow or worse wind/snow warning for the South or Capital region on Sat night or Sun morning? Move Saturday night to Reykjavík or Keflavík.
  • Then Saturday is Seljalandsfoss + Skógafoss only. Leave Skógafoss by 11:40 and you're in Reykjavík about 2:45 PM or Keflavík about 3:30 PM, in daylight. Never drive into the storm.
  • Why Friday? Refundable hotels usually need 24–48 h notice. A late switch may cost one night, and that's worth it.
  • Sunday from Reykjavík: KEF is 45 min map, plan 1 h. Leave by 11:45 AM for a ~1 PM car return (earlier in bad weather). From Keflavík, it's minutes.

Winter safety

  • 4×4 helps you go, not stop. Ask Blue for studded tires and drive slowly on ice.
  • Booster seat for your son. It's the law under 135 cm. Rent it from Blue.
  • Reynisfjara: sneaker waves reach dry sand. Stay well back from the shoreline, never turn your back to the sea, and skip the beach if it's closed or there's a warning.
  • Microspikes for both of you. Waterfall paths are icy.
  • Glacier: look from the viewpoint only. Never walk on it without a guide.
  • In the car: warm layers, hats, gloves, snacks, water, a power bank and charger, and offline Google Maps. Keep the tank over half.
🚨 If roads turn bad ▾
  • Slow down. Pull into a gas station or town, never stop on the road.
  • Check umferdin.is or call 1777 (6:30 AM–10 PM). Don't drive past a closed-road sign.
  • Check wind warnings on en.vedur.is. Wait it out. Turning back is fine.
  • Emergency: 112. Install the 112 Iceland app and leave a travel plan on safetravel.is.
  • Gas pumps need a card PIN, or buy a prepaid N1 or Orkan card.

Is this realistic?

Yes, for you and your son, if you use the skip lists.

Thu and Sun are easy. Fri is moderate. Sat is the long one, about 4 h 35 of planned driving with you as the only driver, so respect the 3 PM turnaround and turn back early if the weather turns.

Expect weather to cost you a stop or two. Book everything refundable (lagoon, hotels, Friðheimar, car), check the road and weather sites each morning, and let making the flight beat every sight.

Checked facts

✅ What I verified (Oct 21, 2026) ▾

✅ confirmed on an official or current site · ℹ️ third-party or conflicting info · ⚠️ recent news. Nothing here is a live status, so re-check before you go.

  • ✅ Blue Lagoon is open on normal winter hours, 8 AM–10 PM (out of the water by 9:30 PM). Pre-booking is essential. No closure notice as of Oct 21, 2026. source
  • ✅ Blue Lagoon kids: minimum age 2, floaties required up to age 8, 11 and under 2,000 ISK. source
  • ✅ Blue Lagoon cancellation (individual bookings): more than 24 h notice = 100% refund, under 24 h = no refund. Date/time changes may cost more, and a downgrade isn't refunded. If the lagoon cancels for force majeure (weather, natural disasters), its terms say no compensation or refund is payable. source
  • ✅ Volcano: no eruption right now. Magma is still building under Svartsengi, and a new eruption could come with under 1 h of warning. The lagoon closes and evacuates if one starts. Book refundable. source
  • ✅ Sky Lagoon: minimum age 12. source
  • ✅ Laugardalslaug pool: Thu 6:30 AM–10 PM, weekends 8 AM–10 PM. source
  • ✅ Perlan exhibitions incl. ice cave: 9 AM–9 PM, free parking. source
  • ✅ Hallgrímskirkja: 10 AM–5 PM in winter, last tower entry 4:45. Tower 1,500 ISK adult, 200 ISK age 7–16, tickets on site only. source
  • ✅ Þingvellir: no entry fee. Parking 1,000 ISK per car per day, read by camera; pay at a machine or checkit.is. source
  • ✅ Friðheimar: greenhouse kitchen open 11:30 AM–4 PM daily, book ahead (Dineout). Kids 6–14 get the soup buffet at half price. The wine bar next door (noon–10 PM) needs no booking. source
  • ℹ️ Geysir: free entry. Parking about 1,000 ISK via Parka. source
  • ℹ️ Gullfoss: free entry, and the upper viewpoint is open all year. The lower path is often closed in winter. Parking info conflicts (free vs. about 1,080 ISK via Parka), so follow the signs. source
  • ✅ Seljalandsfoss: parking 900 ISK per car. The path behind the falls is typically closed in winter. source
  • ℹ️ Skógafoss: free. Parking about 1,000 ISK via Parka. source
  • ℹ️ Sólheimajökull: parking about 750 ISK via Parka. The viewpoint is a 15–20 min walk. source
  • ⚠️ Reynisfjara: RÚV reported on Oct 15, 2026 that several tourists, including a child, were caught by waves. Landowners activated their safety plan and set up closure posts. The lit warning sign was removed after erosion, so obey posts and staff. source
  • ✅ Kerið: 700 ISK per person, free parking, "open when the sun is shining" (≈10 AM–5 PM in winter). source
  • ✅ Car seats: every child under 135 cm needs a car seat or booster, by Icelandic law. source
  • ✅ Road info line 1777, open 6:30 AM–10 PM. Emergency 112. source

The sights

Blue Lagoon

Milky-blue hot lagoon in a lava field, 20 min from the airport.

👦 Floaties up to age 8 (free). Kids' ticket 2,000 ISK.

Hallgrímskirkja

Reykjavík's rocket-shaped church with an elevator to the top.

👦 Tower 200 ISK for kids.

Perlan

Museum with a real ice cave and a northern-lights show.

👦 Indoors, great for a dark or stormy afternoon.

Þingvellir

Walk through the crack between two continents.

👦 Bring ice cleats.

Geysir & Strokkur

Strokkur shoots boiling water up every few minutes.

👦 Count down the eruptions; stay behind ropes.

Gullfoss

Huge two-step waterfall into a canyon.

👦 Upper path only in winter.

Friðheimar

Lunch inside a tomato greenhouse.

👦 Book a table; horses next door.

Seljalandsfoss

60 m waterfall right by the road.

👦 View from the front; the path behind is closed in winter.

Skógafoss

Giant curtain waterfall, often with a rainbow.

👦 Walk up close to feel the spray.

Sólheimajökull

Glacier tongue, short walk from the parking lot.

👦 Look, don't step on the ice.

Reynisfjara

Black sand, basalt columns, sea stacks.

👦 Hold hands. View from well back; dry sand isn't safe.

Vík

Tiny village with the red-roof church.

👦 Optional. Fuel up in Hella, not here.

Kerið

Red volcanic crater with a lake.

👦 Short rim walk; edges unfenced.

Northern lights

Peak season; needs clear skies.

👦 Check the en.vedur.is aurora forecast each evening.
